🌐 Web query:

`Does JavaScript `parseInt("0g", 16)` return `NaN`, or does it partially parse and return `0`?`

💡 Result:

JavaScript parseInt("0g", 16) partially parses and returns 0. According to the MDN documentation for parseInt, if parseInt encounters a character in the input string that is not a valid numeral in the specified radix, it ignores it and all succeeding characters and returns the integer value parsed up to that point. Here, "0" is a valid hex digit (value 0), and "g" is invalid for base 16 (valid digits are 0-9, a-f, A-F), so it parses "0" and returns 0. This behavior is consistent across ECMAScript implementations, as confirmed by the specification description referenced in multiple sources including MDN and Stack Overflow discussions on similar cases like parseInt('dsff66',16) returning 13 (parsing 'd'). Examples like parseInt("xyz", unspecified) return NaN because the first character 'x' is invalid without radix, but with radix 16 and first valid digit, it parses prefix. It does not return NaN because the first non-whitespace character "0" can be converted to a number in radix 16; NaN only if the first character cannot.

Citations:

- 1: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/parseInt.
- 2: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/26017371/why-does-parseintdsff66-16-return-13
- 3: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/parseInt
- 4: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29781856/why-does-javascript-parseint0x4a-return-the-same-as-parseint0x4avv

**Reject partial hex parsing for `--mem` bytes.**

Line 479 uses `parseInt(..., 16)` and Line 480 only checks `NaN`; malformed pairs like `"0g"` are accepted as `0`, so invalid input can pass silently.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    for (let j = 0; j < hexStr.length; j += 2) {
-      const byte = parseInt(hexStr.slice(j, j + 2), 16);
-      if (Number.isNaN(byte)) {
-        throw new Error(`--mem entry ${i} has invalid hex byte at position ${j}: "${hexStr.slice(j, j + 2)}".`);
-      }
-      data.push(byte);
-    }
+    for (let j = 0; j < hexStr.length; j += 2) {
+      const pair = hexStr.slice(j, j + 2);
+      if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}$/.test(pair)) {
+        throw new Error(`--mem entry ${i} has invalid hex byte at position ${j}: "${pair}".`);
+      }
+      data.push(Number.parseInt(pair, 16));
+    }
```
</details>
